novelty_flags.one_line: The closest same-design published comparator is ImbensQinWager2025's common-variance BAE large-deviation analysis, but this theorem's gap names only Wang et al.; add an explicit theorem/section comparison identifying exactly which heteroskedastic contraction and equality steps remain new.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes common Gaussian variance, studies batched arm elimination including a two-batch eliminate-one example, and proves sufficient conditions for universal dominance over uniform completely randomized trials.
For known heterogeneous Gaussian variances, GNA-EBA is analyzed against a worst-case equal-gap criterion; Theorem 4.4 matches the lower and upper bounds in the equal-gap class.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 4, Theorem 1 and remarks (a)--(c); p. 10, Conclusion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 transfers an allocation-proportion LDP upper bound to an empirical-reward LDP upper bound and explicitly states that it does not yield a complete LDP for adaptive algorithms.
SHVar assumes known heterogeneous reward variances and Theorem 3 supplies a finite-budget exponential misidentification-probability upper bound.
The note frames instance-dependent asymptotic complexity in fixed-budget best-arm identification as an open problem.
Tri-BBAI is a fixed-confidence, three-batch asymptotic sample-complexity result, distinct from the proposal's fixed-budget exponent criterion.
The paper gives an impossibility relative to the stronger mean-aware static oracle for K at least 3 in one-parameter natural exponential families.
